ai_show_review.summary: Feedback sandwich bookends a wild Caution jam and rare Space‑Eleven‑Stephen
ai_show_review.blurb: The early‑show bursts from feedback into a chaotic set highlighted by a monster Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) and the rare Space > The Eleven > St. Stephen sequence. Jerry’s guitar is blazing through lo‑fi tape, while the drummers are barely audible but the rhythmic drive shines.
ai_show_review.review: June 14, 1968 at the Fillmore East captures the Grateful Dead at a fever‑pitch experimental peak. Even though both surviving recordings are audience tapes with muffled drums and buried bass, the performance cuts through the haze: a feedback sandwich opens and closes the set, framing a high‑energy journey that includes an almost 24‑minute Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks), the legendary Space → The Eleven → St. Stephen trek, and a wild Alligator → Lovelight transition. Garcia’s “unconscious” guitar tone is startlingly clear and dominant, delivering blistering leads that carry the show despite the primitive recording quality. Phil’s bass slips into the background, but occasional vocal harmonies surface, while the dual drummers are felt more than heard. For fans of the band’s early‑era psychedelia, this tape is a gritty, essential snapshot of the Dead pushing boundaries on stage.

best_recording.reason: Despite lo‑fi fidelity, Jerry’s guitar cuts through clearly and the iconic feedback sandwich is most intact, making it the clearest representation of the show.

key_highlights: Monster Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) jam (~24 min)
Rare Space → The Eleven → St. Stephen sequence
Alligator → Lovelight transition adds a surprising twist
Feedback sandwich framing the set gives the show a primal arc

band_performance.Jerry: Dominant, almost “unconscious” guitar tone that blazes through the mix; intensity and volume are extraordinary.
band_performance.Phil: Bass largely buried on these tapes; occasional vocal harmonies noted but little bass commentary possible.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums faint and often inaudible, yet the rhythmic drive is felt throughout the set.
band_performance.Billy: Similarly low‑level in the recording; the dual‑drum foundation underpins the chaos despite being hard to hear.
